name: security-runtime-proof
truth_boundary: This contract proves only the checked authentication, authorization, anti-spoofing, token-rotation, and credential-storage behavior observed in the GitHub-hosted Docker Compose environment. It is not a penetration test, formal security audit or certification, production-secret/KMS validation, load/DoS testing, Kubernetes security validation, or physical-PC validation.

checks.claim: Gateway actuator health reports UP before the security exercise.
Identity-service actuator health reports UP before the security exercise.
Registration returns an access token, opaque refresh token, and API_CONSUMER account context.
A protected gateway route rejects a request without a bearer token with HTTP 401.
Caller-supplied X-Aetheris identity headers do not bypass bearer-token authentication.
The issued API_CONSUMER access token can perform its authorized users:read request.
A valid API_CONSUMER token plus forged ADMIN/scopes headers cannot obtain users:write and is rejected with HTTP 403.
A signature-tampered access token is rejected with HTTP 401.
The opaque refresh token cannot be used as an access bearer token on a protected route.
The registered password is persisted only as a BCrypt cost-12 hash rather than plaintext.
The raw refresh bearer token is absent from the persisted refresh-token values.
The persisted refresh-token value matches the SHA-256 digest of the issued raw refresh token.
Refreshing rotates the credential and returns a distinct replacement refresh token.
After rotation, the original token hash is marked revoked in PostgreSQL.
The replacement token is represented by a distinct SHA-256 hash that remains active after rotation.
Replaying the already-rotated refresh token is rejected with HTTP 401.
